$comment: pe UCRT migration Phase 1 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the pe `library` binding moved msvcrt.dll -> ucrtbase.dll. P1 flips only the STATELESS descriptors — the migration's safe unit is a CO-STATE GROUP (a heap ptr / FILE* / CRT fd / errno / static tm created by one CRT and read by the other corrupts SILENTLY), and a ctype classifier neither creates nor consumes any such object: it maps a value to a value. All 13 symbols verified present in the live ucrtbase.dll export table (objdump -p) per the EAGER-IMPORT LAW (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT: DSS imports EVERY declared shipped extern whether referenced or not, so an absent name breaks the binary LOAD with 0xC0000139). ★ LOCALE IS THE NON-OBVIOUS RISK HERE, and it was PROVEN not asserted: every ctype classifier consults the CRT's current locale (UCRT's __acrt_locale_data), which is normally populated by the EXE's UCRT startup that DSS's startup-less pe entry does NOT run — an unpopulated table would make isalpha() silently answer wrong (a silent-miscompile class). The Phase-0 pre-flight ran a pe64 --config=release binary bound to ucrtbase.dll asserting the exact C-locale answers in BOTH directions (isalpha('A')/isdigit('7')/isspace('\t')/isupper/islower/ispunct positive AND isalpha('4')/isdigit('x')/isupper('k') negative, plus toupper/tolower mappings): ucrtbase's locale data self-initializes on DLL-attach and every answer is correct. Same run under msvcrt.dll for contrast — identical. See math.json for the first ucrtbase binding (C99 math, Phase-0-of-record). ★★ LANE-O (D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT, the pe `kind: object` half): `_mbcasemap` IS THE FIRST `kind: object` DATA ROW THE pe AXIS HAS EVER HAD — before it, all 7 object rows in the whole corpus were elf or macho (stdio stdout/stderr/stdin + __std{in,out,err}p, unistd __environ), so the pe data-import binding model had descriptor coverage of exactly ZERO names and was witnessed only by source-side externs. Its accessor `__p__mbcasemap` ships beside it because the WITNESS NEEDS AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE, not because a consumer asked. ★ PLACEMENT, chosen with a stated cost (the setlocale-in-stdlib.json and Darwin-malloc_zone-in-stdlib.json precedent): `_mbcasemap` is a <mbctype.h> name, so this <ctype.h> descriptor now declares a name the REAL <ctype.h> does not. The alternative — a new minimal mbctype.json — is STRICTLY WORSE, because a descriptor SHADOWS its header TOTALLY (src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp:75-79): today a future #include <mbctype.h> still reaches the REAL SDK header via D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK, and a partial descriptor would REGRESS that, while a COMPLETE mbctype.json would owe the whole _MB_CP_*/_MS/_MP/_M1/_M2 constant domain and the _mbctype table with no consumer to witness any of it (#include <mbctype.h> appears NOWHERE in the repo — grepped). ctype.json is the smallest semantic distance (MBCS character classification is the multibyte sibling of the classifiers above) and placement is organizational anyway: the consuming oracle scans symbols[].name across ALL descriptors. ★ NO per-symbol `library` override, deliberately: this file's own map ALREADY binds pe -> ucrtbase.dll, so an override would mint a SECOND OWNER of a fact declared once and let the two drift (the setlocale rule). ★ EAGER-IMPORT DISCHARGE (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT — every pe program that includes <ctype.h> now imports BOTH names, so a declared non-export would break EVERY such binary's LOAD with 0xC0000139): ✔MEASURED 2026-08-10 on the live C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100.8875 with TWO CONCURRING INSTRUMENTS, GNU objdump 2.42 -p (0-BASED name-table index) and MSVC dumpbin 14.44.35207 -exports (real ORDINALS), over all 2,484 exports: `_mbcasemap` ORDINAL 527 RVA 0x001397E0, `__p__mbcasemap` ORDINAL 89 RVA 0x000C1D00. `_mbcasemap` is ALSO a msvcrt.dll export (ordinal 520, of 1,330), so this row survives a revert of the CRT flip; `__p__mbcasemap` is ucrtbase-ONLY (ABSENT from msvcrt on both instruments), which is stated because it is the half that would NOT survive one. ⚠ NOTATION: objdump prints a 0-based index and the PE OrdinalBase is 1, so index 526 IS ordinal 527 (the `_set_abort_behavior` caveat in stdlib.json). ★ `_mbcasemap` is one of exactly TWO non-code exports in the entire ucrtbase image (the other is `_wctype`, ordinal 1951, which is in .rdata and declared in no ucrt header at all); it lives in `.data` at RVA 0x138000..0x13A623 whose section flags are 0xC0000040 = Initialized Data, READ WRITE (dumpbin -headers), which is what makes the witness's store-and-restore leg legal. ★★★ THE SIGNATURE IS `ptr<u8>` AND NOT AN ARRAY, AND THAT IS A MEASURED REFUTATION OF THE OBVIOUS SHAPE — the `environ` lesson (see unistd.json / examples/c/shipped_environ) paid for in the opposite direction. ucrt/mbctype.h:30 declares `extern unsigned char _mbcasemap[];` under _CRT_DECLARE_GLOBAL_VARIABLES_DIRECTLY, so an ARRAY row typed arr<u8,256> looks like the faithful transcription. IT IS WRONG FOR UCRT, proven by a native probe (cl 14.44 /MD, two runs): the ucrtbase `_mbcasemap` DATA export at RVA 0x1397E0 does NOT hold a 256-byte case map — it holds a POINTER, and reading the export as one yields 0x00007FF85DB28730 which is BYTE-EQUAL to `__p__mbcasemap()`'s return on the same run, while the export's own address was 0x00007FF85DB297E0 (the two differ, so the accessor is not &_mbcasemap); the qword at export+8 is another pointer exactly +0x100 away, i.e. this is a POINTER TABLE, and the 256 bytes AT the pointed-to address are a real case map (125 of 256 nonzero). THE MATCHED CONTROL SETTLES IT: legacy msvcrt.dll's `_mbcasemap` (ordinal 520, RVA 0x9E400) IS the table itself — 125 of 256 nonzero, the same population count as ucrtbase's pointed-to table. So the CRT changed the export's SHAPE from array to pointer and the SDK header's direct-declaration arm still describes the msvcrt shape. ⚠ CONSEQUENCE THE NEXT READER MUST NOT RE-DERIVE WRONGLY, AND STATED WITH THE RIGHT OWNER because the obvious phrasing puts it on the wrong one: the ARRAY SHAPE IS SILENTLY WRONG, but the surface that decides it is the SOURCE DECLARATOR, not this row's `signature`. ✔MEASURED by EXERCISING the arm rather than reasoning about it: declaring `extern unsigned char _mbcasemap[];` in examples/c/extern_data_import_pe/main.c COMPILED rc=0 with ZERO diagnostics and the program RAN to exit 4 — the agreement check catching a binding that no gate anywhere would have flagged. MECHANISM: pe64's dataImportBinding got-indirect derefs the .idata slot to the OBJECT's address and an array reference decays THERE via Gep(...,0) (src/lir/lowering/mir_to_lir.cpp:4726-4748 + src/mir/lowering/hir_to_mir.cpp:3245-3264), so `_mbcasemap[0]` reads the first byte of the POINTER (measured 0x30) instead of the case map's first byte (measured 0x00), whereas a `ptr` object takes the second, C-level load and yields the pointer's VALUE. ⚠ SO WHY DOES THE ROW'S TYPE MATTER AT ALL? Two reasons, neither of them type-checking: a descriptor row is a STATEMENT ABOUT THE OBJECT that the next reader and any future `#include <ctype.h>` consumer will believe, and an array row would be a false one; and ⓘ the array form is not even spellable here — src/hir/hir_text.cpp:2022-2024 makes `arr<`'s comma and extent MANDATORY, there is no incomplete-array type text, so a bound would have to be INVENTED. ⚠ WHAT IS *NOT* TRUE, recorded so nobody credits a check that does not exist: this row's `kind` and `signature` are NOT compared against the source declarator on the bare-extern path — realization hands over only the LIBRARY (semantic_analyzer.cpp:14329-14334 drops `real.isFunction`, and `CorpusSymbolRow::isObject` is written and never read), so a mistyped row and a mistyped extern each go undetected independently ⇒ [[D-FFI-SHIPPED-ROW-KIND-NOT-CROSSCHECKED-AGAINST-DECLARATOR]]. ★ REAL MSVC IS WRONG HERE TOO, and worse: linking that same SDK bare-array declaration with cl /MD bound `_mbcasemap` to an IAT SLOT IN THE PROGRAM'S OWN IMAGE (0x00007FF6628530C8, holding the export address), so `_mbcasemap[0]` read 0xE0 — the low byte of the export's address — i.e. MSVC's auto-import of data without __declspec(dllimport) is TWO indirections off from the case map. DSS is one indirection better BECAUSE it derefs the slot, and correct only once the row's type matches the object. That defect is upstream, so it is anchored rather than mirrored: [[D-FFI-UCRT-HEADER-DECLARES-MBCASEMAP-AS-ARRAY]]. ★ WITNESSES: examples/c/extern_data_import_pe RUNS the binding on pe64 (a bare `extern unsigned char *_mbcasemap;` plus an AGREEMENT check against `__p__mbcasemap()` — see that example for why the ladder asserts an agreement instead of a magic value), and examples/c/extern_data_addr_reject_pe pins the fail-loud half.
